A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 44-page DiffBreak paper, including Appendices A–J. Text, rendered-page, and embedded-figure comparisons establish correspondence throughout; visible differences are confined to the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v4 reports original attack evaluations on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet in Sections 4–6 and Tables 1–3, plus gradient experiments, ablations, and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including evaluations of DiffGrad and low-frequency attacks against diffusion-based purification and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: DiffGrad, the majority-vote defense, and the low-frequency attack retain identical procedures and objectives, including Algorithms 1–3 in Appendices D and I.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-10 and ImageNet coverage and the same adversarial image-classification scenarios. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including BPDA, DiffAttack, DiffHammer, and adjoint and surrogate gradient approaches.

E3.justification: The 256-sample evaluations, perturbation budgets, metrics, attack iterations, model configurations, and EOT and majority-vote settings are identical, including the protocols in Appendices E–H.

E4.justification: The gradient diagnostics in Figure 2, evaluation-sample ablation in Appendix H, and qualitative and StAdv comparisons in Appendix J are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix D.2 retains 20 repetitions for the EOT-gradient analysis and 10 repetitions for the surrogate-gradient comparison. Appendix A retains the same disclosure concerning the absence of formal error bars and confidence intervals.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 3 retains 3.13% robust accuracy for the LF attack against DiffPure with CIFAR-10/WideResNet-70-16 under majority vote.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and its Appendix C proof, the DDPM/VP-SDE equivalence in Appendix B, and the mathematical derivations in Appendix D are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about purification vulnerabilities, accurate differentiation, majority-vote robustness, and the effectiveness of low-frequency attacks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of gradient errors and stochasticity, qualifications about perceptual constraints and other modalities, and the limitations in Appendix A are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation instructions, pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware and timing information, and code-access links are identical. Only the arXiv self-link changes to identify v5.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to previous purification defenses and attacks are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v4 dated 21 Nov 2025 to v5 dated 10 Feb 2026. All manuscript prose, headings, terminology, and section ordering remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Rendered pages match outside the textual version/date stamp, and embedded image and figure content is identical.

improvement.justification: The revision updates the arXiv identification stamp and self-link while preserving the entire scientific and explanatory content, including the appendices. It therefore provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in evidence, rigor, clarity, or reproducibility.
